implementation_evidence.limitation: No live OpenJiuwen engine, gateway, CLI, model, session, stream, tool, approval, reconnect, or artifact traversal is verified.

boundary.authority: Agent Relay session/runtime remains the authority for identity, leases, policy, approvals, persistence, retries, and completion.
boundary.transport: No OpenJiuwen wire protocol or gateway is assumed by this contract. A future adapter must use an explicitly supported local SDK or a separately pinned protocol.
boundary.network: Live network access is disabled by default; contract tests use deterministic replay fixtures only.
boundary.credentials: Credentials are opaque references owned by the selected connection/profile. They must never appear in provider options, logs, events, fixtures, or process arguments.

capabilities.evidence: agent-core describes Python SDK agent creation and the ReActAgent/WorkflowAgent surfaces.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: INCOMPATIBLE when the pinned SDK cannot construct the requested agent or model.

capabilities.evidence: agent-core describes workflow orchestration, graph execution, component jumps, and state recovery.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: UNSUPPORTED; Agent Relay does not import OpenJiuwen workflow graphs into its durable workflow authority.

capabilities.evidence: agent-core describes streaming output and streaming transfer between components.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: UNSUPPORTED when the selected SDK invocation cannot provide ordered, bounded deltas.

capabilities.evidence: agent-core describes tool components and local tools calling external services.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: UNSUPPORTED unless every external effect is surfaced as an Agent Relay approval before execution.

capabilities.evidence: agent-core describes state interruption and recovery, but the exact durable token and replay semantics are not yet pinned.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: UNKNOWN_OUTCOME; never retry automatically when delivery or completion cannot be established.

capabilities.evidence: The pinned public sources do not establish a stable provider-neutral session-history protocol for an external adapter.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: UNSUPPORTED with a detail-free user-visible explanation.

capabilities.evidence: Tool capability is documented, but an authoritative OpenJiuwen approval handshake suitable for Agent Relay has not been established.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: UNSUPPORTED; tools requiring approval must fail closed before invocation.

capabilities.evidence: The pinned sources do not establish a safe, provider-owned changed-file manifest with revision and digest semantics.
capabilities.unsupported_outcome: UNSUPPORTED; Agent Relay must not infer changes from arbitrary tool output.

invariants.rule: Endpoint, model, agent, timeout, and replay limits are allowlisted, finite, and size-bounded before SDK invocation.
Events contain opaque session/turn identifiers and bounded text; credentials, prompts, routes, and raw SDK objects are excluded.
Unknown, unsupported, malformed, unauthorized, or expired tool/effect requests are rejected before external I/O.
A stream must expose monotonic sequence identity and terminal closure; gaps become a failure, not silently reordered output.
A timeout after provider submission becomes an explicit unknown outcome and is never automatically replayed.
OpenJiuwen state is an adapter observation; Agent Relay owns durable session identity, policy, approval, and completion state.

deterministic_test_plan.scenario: Validate official repository URLs, immutable revision shape, and license evidence.
Reject duplicate capability IDs, unknown statuses, missing mappings, and unsupported claims without evidence.
Reject oversized endpoints, credentials in options, invalid timeout values, and unbounded model/agent identifiers.
Replay ordered deltas, duplicate sequence numbers, gaps, malformed events, and missing terminal closure.
Reject tool/effect events without explicit approval and preserve unknown delivery as non-retryable.
Assert fixtures contain no secrets, private paths, host addresses, raw prompts, or provider transcripts.
